key_insight: Stream3D converts a frozen view-conditioned 3D generator into a streaming system by adding an evidential memory that fuses sequential monocular views, producing temporally consistent 3D reconstructions without retraining the base model.
problem_solved: Frame-by-frame use of single-view 3D generators on long monocular streams yields severe temporal inconsistency and flicker; Stream3D addresses stable multi-view fusion across time with a training-free wrapper.
method: Training-free streaming wrapper that sits on top of an existing frozen view-conditioned 3D generator and processes incoming frames sequentially.
Evidential memory: maintain per-voxel (or per-element) beliefs and uncertainty and update them with each new view using evidential/Bayesian-style fusion to resolve conflicts and accumulate consensus.
Temporal query & render: query the fused memory conditioned on the current camera/view to produce consistent 3D outputs each frame, preserving up-to-date detail while avoiding flicker.
impact: Enables robust, temporally coherent 3D reconstruction from long monocular videos without retraining, making high-quality multi-view generation practical for AR/VR, robotics, and dataset capture pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input video → evidential memory (belief & uncertainty) → frozen 3D generator → temporally consistent renders
Before/after sequence: frame-by-frame reconstructions showing flicker from naive approach vs. stable Stream3D outputs
Memory visualization: heatmaps of per-voxel belief and uncertainty evolving over time as new views arrive
Quantitative chart: temporal consistency metric (e.g., IoU or LPIPS) across frames comparing frame-wise baseline and Stream3D
paper_title: Stream3D: Sequential Multi-View 3D Generation via Evidential Memory
paper_authors: Kaichen Zhou, Zeyang Bai, Xinhai Chang, Mengyu Wang, Paul Liang
